evidence.field: 形義通解；甲骨、金文、篆文構形與用例
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 星 as deriving from 晶, which depicts stars arranged in a group, with 生 as phonetic; it gives the original sense as stars. It cites an oracle-bone reading of 星 as 晴 in 《合集》15625反 (“庚辰星(晴)”), a Western Zhou bronze inscription 麓伯簋 using 星 in a personal name, and Warring States bamboo and Han silk examples where 星 writes 腥. It also reports later scattered/numerous senses. These are the entry’s interpretations and examples, not proof of a complete sense chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：星

evidence.field: 說文釋形；字樣說明；釋義
evidence.text: The entry quotes 《說文》 for 曐: “从晶，生聲,” followed by an alternative pictographic analysis; it says 星 is a shortened form of 曐. It gives the word’s star sense and later meanings such as dispersed/scattered and numerous, with literary citations. This records the lexicon’s account and cited usage, not dated first attestations for each extension.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》：星

evidence.source: 國學大師字形演變 compilation
evidence.text: The compilation describes two oracle-bone forms as star-like signs plus 生, and later forms as 晶 simplified to 日 with 生 retained as sound. It lists oracle-bone examples, a Western Zhou 麓伯星父簋, Warring States Chu forms, Shuowen forms and Qin slips. This conflicts with a 晶-first, 生-added-later sequence reported elsewhere; the page alone does not resolve whether the disagreement concerns different forms or analysis.
evidence.title: 星字形演变字源

evidence.field: Old Chinese and Middle Chinese reconstruction table; 星
evidence.text: The inspected 2014 reconstruction table gives 星 xīng, Middle Chinese seng, Old Chinese *s-tsʰˤeŋ, gloss “star.” These are Baxter–Sagart system-specific forms and support a documented reading comparison, but do not independently establish the historical graphic role of 生.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1

evidence.field: Old Chinese and Middle Chinese reconstruction table; 晶
evidence.text: The inspected table gives 晶 jīng, Middle Chinese tsjeng, Old Chinese *tseŋ, gloss “bright, limpid.” This comparison is in the same reconstruction system as 星; differing initials and the phonetic component analysis should not be collapsed into a claim that 晶 is 星’s sound component.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1

evidence.field: 聲韻資料；星 and 生 comparison
evidence.text: The character entry identifies 生 as 星’s phonetic and links to the 生 entry. The input’s local Baxter–Sagart rows give 星 *s-tsʰˤeŋ and 生 *sreŋ (with listed variants), so those rows do not justify silently treating the two as identical or merging other reconstruction systems. The searched official table is accessible for 星, but this evidence item does not assert a table row for 生.
evidence.kind: component phonetic account; reconstructed comparison scoped to supplied local rows
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：星

gaps: The reviewed paleographic accounts disagree about early form sequence: one account says Shang oracle forms already combine star imagery and 生, while the traditional 晶 + 生 analysis and another account suggest a 晶-based form with 生 as phonetic. No corruption or scribal error is established.
No visual inspection of glyph pixels was performed. The Commons candidate is a modern SVG redraw; it must not be captioned as an artifact photograph.
CUHK reports 《合集》15625反 as a clear-weather use and notes the 《詩經》 phrase 星言夙駕 has interpretive debate. These do not establish the earliest occurrence of every sense or a secure semantic chronology.

The listed early evidence distinguishes star meaning, a Western Zhou personal-name use, a disputed clear-weather reading, and later graph borrowing for 腥. Intermediate semantic links and first occurrence dates for later scattered/numerous meanings remain unestablished.

Unihan character-specific pages for U+661F and U+751F returned internal errors. Supplied local kMandarin rows are xīng and shēng; local Baxter–Sagart rows give 星 *s-tsʰˤeŋ and 生 *sreŋ with a variant note, but only 星’s official table row was externally verified. Do not treat these reading comparisons alone as proof of 生’s phonetic function.
No independently recoverable ancient pronunciation/name for a depicted star object was established or needed: the analysis treats 生 as a sound component in the graph, not a whole-graph phonetic loan.

Sinica chardb character-specific evolution page was inspected as evidence lead but states All Rights Reserved; no image asset was selected from it. No clear permission basis for a versioned bulk extract was established.

items.period: Shang period (script-style identification on Commons page; modern digital redraw)
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of a Shang-style 星 form, presented by the source as combining star-related imagery with 生. It illustrates a proposed early form, not an excavated inscription photograph.
items.alt: Black line drawing of an archaic Chinese character form on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: The file is specifically identified as 星 in Shang oracle-script style and the page names its model and reuse terms. It can illustrate the early-form proposal while the textual evidence records disagreement about whether 生 was present in the earliest forms.
items.rights: The Commons description states a public-domain dedication for the SVG representation, for international use.

limitations.text: This is a modern redraw attributed to the HB2813 source form, not a photograph of an ancient bone; the account of which components the earliest graph contains is disputed.
